Decide for each numbered item whether it is RELEVANT to a study of SIPs (systematic investment plans in mutual funds, incl. auto-invest / monthly mutual-fund investing) with three questions:
  (A) Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
  (B) What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting (checking returns, increasing, reducing, skipping, redeeming, switching, sticking with it)?
  (C) What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?

RELEVANT = the text describes the writer's own (or other investors') SIP experience, motives, expectations, behaviour or decisions that speak to A, B or C - including payment/mandate/app problems that make a SIP miss or stop.
NOT RELEVANT = generic praise or complaints about the app, stock trading only, SIPs merely named with nothing about motives/expectations/behaviour/decisions, spam or promotion, thanks to a video creator, or bare how-to questions with no personal situation.
The context line (video or forum topic title) is background only; judge the text.

Return a JSON array with one object per item: [{"i": <item number>, "relevant": true|false}]

Overcomplicated redesign is ruining a once-simple app
As a long-time Upstox user, I am extremely disappointed with the direction this app is heading. I am not a daily day trader; I simply invest manage my portfolio, invest, and close the app until the next time. Upstox used to be great for this, but the recent design changes have turned a once-clean platform into a cluttered mess.
In the name of "upgrading," they have made basic navigation unnecessarily complicated. Finding standard services and essential portfolio details takes way too much effort now. The home page is crowded with irrelevant features that many of us never asked for:
 Unsolicited F&O & Strategy Tools: Pushing complex options trading strategies and trade ideas directly onto the homepage clutter is useless for long-term investors. Anyone who actively trades F&O already knows what tools they need; forcing it on everyone else just creates noise.
 Intrusive "Expert Advice" & Mutual Fund SIPs: Putting aggressive recommendations front and center makes the app feel cheap and chaotic. If someone wants to start a Mutual Fund SIP, they will intentionally navigate to the MF section—it doesn't need to take over the main screen.
Upstox needs to realize that adding more clutter isn't an upgrade—it's bad UX. Making the app hard to understand for simple, long-term investors will only drive customers away. If this bloated interface continues to prioritize pushed features over clean usability, I will consider closing my Demat

Don’t invest in Upstox. Very bad customer services.
